title: Upper Body focused 5 days PPL + sprints program review
summary: NH reviews a viewer's (Daquan) upper-body-focused push/pull/legs program with sprints as the second leg day. He criticises drop sets bolted onto static 4x5s, redundant chest and lat exercises, missing rear and medial delt and long head triceps work, supinated rows and supersetting strength work, and proposes a leaner leg day built around back squats.
claims: Using only sprints or plyometrics for legs is fine if it works for you, though strength training is always an asset for athletes
Running push A then push B back to back damages recovery and performance; alternate push, pull, push, pull
Adding a drop set to a static 4x5 makes little sense; just do a 5x5, or do 1-3 heavy sets of five and let the drop-set sets evolve
One heavy set followed by several lower-intensity sets, such as 1 heavy deadlift set then 3x4, works well for progression
4x8 is a very good rep range for overhead press; presses need lots of volume
Don't do both cable press and dumbbell flies in one day; pick one and rotate them like the main bench variations
A typical 'push day' that only trains chest and front delts is a bro split that lacks medial and rear delt work and risks imbalance and injury
Make the two overhead press days clearly different: if one is 4x8 (32 reps), make the other about 3x5 (15) instead of 5x5 (25)
Overhead press is a lift where progression is tough
Stacking exercises that pre-fatigue the same muscle must be intentional; otherwise it damages progression
Choose cables over the pec deck; the pec deck can be dangerous for the shoulders
3x10 face pulls is on the low side; go for 3-4 sets of 15, you can never do enough
Barbell overhead extension 3x10 is a perfect rep range for long head triceps
Ditch triceps kickbacks: gravity makes them poor for progression, they may hurt tendons and don't fit any movement pattern
Static rep ranges are acceptable on weighted chin-ups because you replicate the same ROM and technique
Avoid supinated-grip rows; they can tear the biceps and limit the weight
Four lat exercises back to back is wasted time; you end up using unchallenging weights. Keep weighted chins and pick one other
Move one biceps exercise to push day: higher frequency gives more recovery and better progression than two curls back to back
Farmer's walks are taxing; use them as strength work at the start of a session or give them their own day, not after everything
Athletes should include a submaximal pull from the floor, even trap bar, to learn to transfer force from floor to hips; it's a good pull-day opener
Without floor pulls and with supinated rows, traps, rhomboids, upper back and lower back end up underdeveloped
Squats and deadlifts carry over to sport better than farmer's walks, where the joints are locked
Never open a workout with rows, especially a supinated 5x5; static ranges and low weight on rows are a bad idea
3x6-10 is an excellent rep range for curls
Never superset strength work, even with a different muscle; it hurts focus and adds a variable to progression
If a day has both a floor pull and a squat, the later one suffers; open legs with back squats for 3-4 sets of 6-8 and put deadlifts on pull day
Legs are simple to program: squats and deadlift variations are all you need; use machines only if you can't back squat
Lying leg curls are one of the few good machine exercises; they take the hamstrings past the ROM of a hip hinge
Leg days end up shorter than upper body days because they carry more tonnage and fatigue the whole system
Do the back squat drop set paused to cover hamstrings; hip thrusts also train hamstrings
For a weak chest, focus on progressing a few key exercises rather than doing a thousand random sets; push-ups can be added at the end of push days
exercises: can be dangerous for shoulders; prefer cables
rear delts; only real source of rear delt work
poor for progression, may hurt tendons; drop it
risk of biceps tear, limits load
do at the start or on its own day
teaches force transfer floor to hips
